transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (BlueWave ML Eng), Daniel Cho (BlueWave Backend Lead), Lena Ortiz (BlueWave Product)
-- Auto-generated summary (brief): Weekly POC sync focused on caching tuning. Reviewed KV/prefix cache hit rates, prompt reuse strategies, and next experiments. Agreed on tests and dates; Redwood to share pricing and run scalability run.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep it to 45. Marco and I will run through the caching numbers and then we'll go through Priya's questions.
[00:12] Priya: Hey, thanks. we got a quick schedule conflict so appreciate keeping tight.
[00:16] Marco: Cool. Quick reminder this is the weekly POC check-in for caching. We pushed the KV cache instrumentation on Monday and started collecting hit-rate metrics across the dev traffic shape.
[00:28] Daniel: Great, the sample traffic we gave should be coming through? it's the one with spikes at 9am and 2pm right?
[00:34] Marco: Yep that's the one. We ran two runs: baseline with no prefix cache and then prefix + KV enabled with 256k TTL for prefix entries.
[00:46] Sofia: I'll just surface the headline numbers first. Overall KV hit-rate across the 72-hour run was about 37% on average, prefix cache contribution about 22% of served tokens, aggregate end-to-end token cost down ~18% in the test env.
[01:05] Priya: 37% seems a bit lower than we hoped based on earlier sim. Where are misses concentrated?
[01:12] Marco: Good question. Looking at the breakdown, the hit-rate is high for the high-frequency prompts — our top 200 prompt templates — those are hitting at ~68%. The long tail (ad-hoc prompts and customer-specific prompts) is under 10%. So the distribution matches a Zipf-like pattern.
[01:30] Lena: when you say prompt templates, do you mean preface templates or full prompt bodies? how are we defining reuse?
[01:36] Marco: We tagged a "prompt template" when the prefix — the first 128 tokens — matched across requests. We saw most reuse in instruction/boilerplate parts vs user-specific inserted fields. So prefix caching helps a lot when your product uses standard system + few-shot patterns.
[01:55] Daniel: Any weirdness with KV cache eviction or staleness? we worry about user-specific context leaking or stale completions.
[02:02] Marco: We set TTL at 24 hours for user-scoped entries in one run and 256k tokens (approx) TTL for shared prefixes; eviction looked normal. No observed leak of user identifiers in cache; but we recommended adding per-tenant namespace keys — we documented that.
[02:21] Sofia: Quick note — BlueWave asked about retention and encryption; Marco, remind them about KMS integration and how logs are audited.
[02:28] Marco: Right. In Private/Dedicated we support customer KMS for cache metadata encryption and audit logs stream to your SIEM. See security doc: https://redwood.example.com/security/bluewave-poc (shared).
[02:42] Priya: thanks. can we talk about the hit-rate experiment specifics? what qualifies as a cacheable hit?
[02:49] Marco: Our definition for this POC: a cache hit is when the KV lookup returns a prefix KV that eliminates >=1 token generation step (i.e., reused autoregressive state), so we count any match that allowed us to skip forward in the model's decoding graph. There's a small chance of false positives when paraphrases are similar — transcription fuzziness — but we estimated false positives <2% with exact prefix hashing.
[03:12] Priya: ok, good. Also the team observed some latency variance when a hit occurs vs miss — was that expected?
[03:18] Marco: Yes. Hits are slightly faster on average, but there is a small added lookup latency of ~6-12ms in the control path for KV read when using remote cache. For local in-memory cache it's ~1-3ms. Overall net latency benefited when cache allowed skipping large decoding windows.
[03:39] Daniel: do you have numbers for p95/p99? our SLA concerns are at p99.
[03:44] Marco: p95 improved by ~40ms in the cached run; p99 showed mixed results — small wins in steady traffic but we saw a few tail spikes likely due to cache missstorms during burst events. We're working on prefetching heuristics to mitigate missstorms.
[04:03] Sofia: Missstorms meaning many unique prompts at the same time causing high miss-rate and backend thrash, right?
[04:09] Marco: Exactly. For example, when a new marketing campaign hit, unique prompt variety increased, so warm-up is required. We're testing adaptive batching + proactive population for likely prefixes.
[04:24] Priya: On the product side, our main ask is: how do we increase effective reuse? We have a lot of personalization tokens that differ per user.
[04:33] Marco: Two paths: 1) prompt engineering to move variable fields to the end of the prompt so prefixes are more stable; 2) canonicalization — normalize user-specific IDs or remove them from the prompt and pass as metadata to the application layer. Priya, you mentioned earlier you can try template changes?
[04:51] Priya: yes we can. we'll run a quick pass to see if we can move some fields. Might affect downstream parsing though.
[04:58] Lena: any quick wins on the infrastructure side? like increasing prefix length threshold or making a hybrid TTL?
[05:04] Marco: Increasing prefix length helps if reuse is long, but longer prefixes reduce match probability across paraphrases. Hybrid TTLs per-namespace helped in our tests — high-frequency prefixes get longer TTLs. Also LRU eviction tuned to favor shared prefixes.
[05:22] Sofia: We also tested quantized model variants in Dedicated. That reduces per-token cost but it's orthogonal to cache strategy; worth noting when calculating unit economics.
[05:34] Daniel: we saw a slide earlier about cost savings; can you share the spreadsheet again?
[05:38] Sofia: Sure — link to benchmark workbook: https://redwood.example.com/pocs/bluewave/caching-benchmarks (view).
[05:45] Priya: nice. about test coverage — will Marco's 1M session run use real user traffic replay or synthetic?
[05:51] Marco: We'll do both. First pass is a replay of anonymized user sessions you provide; second is a synthetic stress run to simulate burst patterns. We're trying to replicate your morning spike.
[06:03] Priya: timeline?
[06:05] Marco: I'll start the replay today and have initial results by 2026-03-10.
[06:10] Daniel: what about metric invariants? we want to be sure cache doesn't change semantics of responses — like hallucination rates.
[06:17] Marco: We do a quality regression check — run the eval on a holdout prompt set comparing completions with and without cache. So far delta in BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics is negligible; we also add targeted human checks for top 500 templates.
[06:33] Lena: any cases where cache made quality worse?
[06:36] Marco: Rarely, when cache returned slightly stale continuations because the prompt context changed semantics; that's why we added freshness TTL per-template and a freshness score threshold.
[06:50] Priya: ok good. On SSO and compliance — we need SOC2 type II and SSO for pilot users; where do we stand?
[06:58] Sofia: Redwood has SOC2 in prod and we can provide the relevant report under NDA; SSO/SAML is supported for Dedicated and Private control planes. We'll attach the security pack in the follow-up.
[07:12] Priya: can you include audit log detail for cache hits? our privacy team wants visibility into which tenant got a hit.
[07:18] Marco: Yes, per-tenant hit logs are available in the Dedicated control plane; logs include namespace, prefix hash, and timestamp. Payloads are never logged.
[07:30] Daniel: any extra infra requirements for Dedicated for cache? like memory footprint?
[07:35] Marco: We recommend a dedicated in-memory cache layer for low-latency — e.g., 128GB per shard depending on traffic. For shared prefix caches you can also use Redis with local L1 caches. We'll provide a sizing guide.
[07:51] Sofia: Quick check — are there any blockers from BlueWave side to run the 1M session test?
[07:56] Priya: we need to anonymize and share the replay; we'll do that by end of day Friday. Also need the contract language on pilot terms.
[08:06] Sofia: Noted. I'll send pilot terms.
[08:10] Marco: Just to add, one of our experiments was prompt canonicalization — we replaced user IDs with placeholders and saw an effective hit-rate bump from 37% to ~52% for the top templates. That's a low-effort change you might try.
[08:25] Priya: that's promising. any tradeoffs? like loss of personalization?
[08:29] Marco: You'd re-inject user-specific tokens at the end, or keep them as metadata; the generated text still conditions on them if you pass them properly. It's primarily a prompt engineering change.
[08:41] Daniel: about missstorms mitigation — is prefetching safe with user-specific prefixes? won't that pre-populate others' context?
[08:48] Marco: Prefetching is tenant-aware; we prefetch only within namespace and respect privacy. For public templates we can pre-warm across shards.
[08:59] Lena: any notes on rollout strategy? we don't want to flip on cache globally and surprise users.
[09:05] Sofia: We recommend a canary approach — start with 5% of traffic, run quality checks, ramp to 25% then 100% with automated rollback on regression. Redwood Console supports route-based rollouts.
[09:18] Priya: sounds good. A few quick questions from security: do you store plain-text prompts in the cache?
[09:24] Marco: No. Cache keys are hashed; cached state contains only model KV state, no PII. With Dedicated we can encrypt metadata with your KMS.
[09:34] Daniel: ok. let's talk about validation metrics we want to see in the next update.
[09:39] Marco: We'll provide: per-template hit-rate, overall hit-rate, cost delta per 1k tokens, p50/p95/p99 latencies, quality deltas on holdout set, and memory footprint.
[09:52] Priya: can you also add per-tenant breakdown and a list of top 50 templates by volume?
[09:58] Marco: Yep; will include top 50 and a scatter of reuse vs latency.
[10:04] Sofia: Any open concerns on your side?
[10:07] Priya: mainly to ensure the cache doesn't change model outputs and to see concrete numbers on expected cost savings. Also want to ensure Dedicated pricing works for our projected scale.
[10:18] Sofia: We'll send the Dedicated pricing and the cost modeling spreadsheet with your traffic. Marco will run the tests and share results by 2026-03-10.
[10:26] Daniel: Great. One nit — earlier in the doc link you used 'redwood dedicate' — small nit in slide text.
[10:32] Sofia: Thanks, we'll fix that.
[10:35] Marco: Quick last note: for the large-scale run we'll simulate a marketing spike where unique prompts go +3x, that will show missstorm behavior and prefetch efficacy.
[10:45] Priya: ok thanks everyone.
[10:48] Sofia: OK, recap of next steps: Marco runs KV run and shares spreadsheet by 3/10; Sofia sends pilot terms and Dedicated pricing by 3/5; BlueWave provides anonymized replay and prompt set by 3/8. We'll schedule the latency benchmark for the week of 3/9. If no more questions we'll wrap.
[11:05] Priya: Nothing else, thanks.
[11:07] Lena: thanks!
[11:09] Sofia: Thanks all, bye.
